properties.decision:
Anthony asked, 2026-10-01: "should this be done on another branch or should we make it so that reflow2 supports both native mcp and via the command --call?" The recommendation was one reflow2 with both routes, and he answered: "I agree".

WHAT IT MEANS:
- The door work lands on main like any other change, each step through its own short-lived branch and PR (as #617 does).
- Nothing about it lives on a branch that has to be kept merged.
- The planned door improvements are ADDITIONS to the CLI. None changes what an MCP client sees.
properties.name: ACCEPTED 2026-10-01 — one reflow2 serves both routes, native MCP and the `--call` door; no separate long-lived branch for the door
properties.rationale:
`--call` is not a second implementation. call_one_tool (main.rs:731) serves the design to an in-process client over an in-memory pipe and makes the call through the same call_tool path a session uses. Every tool, guard and refusal therefore exists once, and a fix reaches both routes.

A long-lived branch for the door would need every release merged into it and would drift within weeks: two reflow2s that disagree. That is the failure the hub avoids by never keeping two copies of one requirement.

THE ONE REAL COST: served text says "call X", which means `--call X` through the door. It stays true in both readings through two things:
- an instructions file the binary serves, so it cannot go stale;
- a CI probe that drives the door as an agent would, so a change that breaks the terminal route fails the build.
Both are in req:init-installs-the-terminal-route-for-vs-code-and-update-keeps-it-current.
